spec: FINAL_SERVER_AUTHORITATIVE_EXECUTION_PLAN §11 (S11-infra-author)
LIVE STATE CAPTURED 2026-08-15 (read-only, aws s3api get-bucket-cors):
NoSuchCORSConfiguration — this bucket has NO CORS config today. Rollback:
aws s3api delete-bucket-cors --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --region ap-south-1
HONESTY NOTE (repo-is-truth, verified before authoring this file): as of
2026-08-15, NOTHING in src/ performs a direct browser-to-S3 request against
this bucket. grep across S3AttachmentStorageService.cs / S3RawBlobStore.cs /
the receipt+patti capture components found no presigned PUT or GET URL for
attachments or ai-sessions objects — every upload and download is
server-mediated (multipart POST to the API, API does the S3 PutObject; API
streams GET back). The one presigned-URL code path in this codebase
(ExportRequest.PresignedUrl, DPDP export bundles) targets a DIFFERENT,
currently-nonexistent bucket, is opened as a top-level browser navigation
(not fetch/XHR), and does not need CORS even if that bucket existed.
This file is authored per §11's explicit instruction ('plus bucket
policies ... and CORS') as a conservative, GET-only default so a future
direct-to-browser read path (e.g. thumbnail fetch/canvas access) does not
have to wait on an AWS change — but applying it changes nothing observable
today; no code path exercises it. If this stays unused past the next
infra review, that is a signal to remove it rather than carry unused
attack surface.
Scope: GET only. No PUT/POST — this bucket's write path is server-side
only per the honesty note above, and CORS should not be widened to PUT
unless a genuine presigned-upload feature lands (§11 gap register item:
'no presigned upload' is tracked elsewhere, not by this file).
Origins mirror the API's own Cors:AllowedOrigins
(src/AgriSync.Bootstrapper/appsettings.Production.json) — no wildcard.
APPLY (founder only): aws s3api put-bucket-cors --bucket shramsafal-uploads-prod --cors-configuration file://cors-policy.json --region ap-south-1
(apply-config.sh does this as part of the single transaction; strips
_comment first since put-bucket-cors rejects unknown top-level keys.)
